name: Escape Zombie Control
description: A blocked Zombie pummel can be reset by preserving guard, withdrawing the pummeling hand and rebuilding Mission Control or ordinary inside frames.
summary: A blocked Zombie pummel can be reset by preserving guard, withdrawing the pummeling hand and rebuilding Mission Control or ordinary inside frames.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Zombie, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. Zombie is an arm-clearing action from facing guard. The guard player is not escaping a lockdown turtle shell, and turning to turtle is not required.

The bottom player has broken posture and supports a high Mission Control leg. The top player's hand or forearm is still obstructing the intended arm isolation. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): The hand pummel stalls; what can you recover first?
flashcards.answer: Withdraw the failed pummel and preserve guard with an inside frame and short hip escape rather than forcing the clamped arm.
flashcards.answer_line: A shoulder frame and room for the inside knee

plausible: A tighter ankle hold with the forearm still outside
An overhook before their hand leaves the inside
trap: A wrist pull with your elbow reaching past their shoulder

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): What must loosen before lowering the Mission Control leg?
flashcards.answer: Release any loaded neck or arm connection before lowering the controlling leg into an ordinary guard reset.
flashcards.answer_line: The high-leg connection around the upper body

plausible: Only the pummeling hand while keeping the high-leg grip
Only your free hand while the high leg stays taut
trap: Only the knee hug while the head-side grip keeps pulling

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): What lets the high knee lower comfortably?
flashcards.answer: Change your hip angle so the leg lowers through space rather than dragging the ankle against a stationary knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Hip movement that clears the leg's path

plausible: Keeping the hips flat and hauling the foot down
Straightening the leg into the opponent's shoulder
trap: Lowering the ankle before releasing the high-leg grip

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): Where should the pummeling forearm go during recovery?
flashcards.answer: The withdrawn hand becomes a useful inside frame so chest pressure cannot replace the failed arm exchange.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside, ahead of the approaching shoulder

plausible: Around the far side of the opponent's back
Flat on the mat outside your own shoulder
trap: Across your own chest behind their entering shoulder

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): What should the hip escape recover?
flashcards.answer: A short shrimp behind the frame admits the inside knee and rebuilds a facing guard barrier.
flashcards.answer_line: A knee between your torso and the opponent

plausible: Both knees behind you in turtle
A foot high behind the head before knee space
trap: A knee alongside their hip but outside the torso gap

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): When is another Zombie attempt well set up?
flashcards.answer: Re-establish Mission Control posture control and a supported knee before using the free hand for another pummel.
flashcards.answer_line: Posture held low with a supported high leg

plausible: When the opponent sits upright with both frames in
When your foot reaches high but the knee drifts back
trap: When their wrist is exposed but your high leg has slipped

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): Which exchange is actually being reset?
flashcards.answer: Zombie works on the opponent's hand and arm from Mission Control; the bottom player is already facing the opponent.
flashcards.answer_line: A facing guard hand pummel under a high leg

plausible: A facing guard knee hug around an already isolated arm
A facing guard grip change around an already cleared head
trap: A second-leg closure with the hand pummel already complete

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (bottom): Why is turning to turtle unnecessary here?
flashcards.answer: The failed pummel leaves a guard-retention problem; frames and inside knees can be restored without turning away.
flashcards.answer_line: You already face the opponent in guard

plausible: Their hand on the mat has already reversed top and bottom
The high leg has already replaced the inside forearm frame
trap: Their captured arm makes inside knee recovery unnecessary

defender.description: Escape Zombie Control (defender): Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed.
defender.overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Zombie, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. Zombie is an arm-clearing action from facing guard. The guard player is not escaping a lockdown turtle shell, and turning to turtle is not required.

Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed. The free hand working under yours is the cue to recover inside position before the knee hug closes.

Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught. Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control. Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Recover without yanking: Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught.
Rebuild posture gradually: Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control.
Respect the high guard: Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (top): Where should your forearm resist the pummel early?
flashcards.answer: Maintain an inside forearm so the bottom player's hand cannot easily lift yours out toward the mat.
flashcards.answer_line: Between the bodies before their hand gets underneath

plausible: Outside their hip with the elbow flared
Behind their head with the hand hidden
trap: Across your chest with the wrist extended beyond the elbow

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (top): How should the hand and elbow recover together?
flashcards.answer: Recover hand and elbow together instead of leaving the wrist exposed beyond a fixed elbow.
flashcards.answer_line: Bring the whole arm inward through available space

plausible: Retract only the wrist with the elbow pinned outside
Straighten the elbow while the hand remains caught
trap: Turn your chest away to drag the elbow through

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (top): Which cue calls for an early inside-hand recovery?
flashcards.answer: The hand-first pummel attacks the opening under your hand; respond before the bottom player's knee hug encloses the arm.
flashcards.answer_line: Their free hand works beneath your hand

plausible: Their free foot settles on the floor
Their high leg has already lowered to the waist
trap: Their free hand returns to frame your shoulder

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (top): Where should the recovered elbow finish?
flashcards.answer: An elbow recovered toward the ribs can frame inside before the New York knee hug fixes it outside.
flashcards.answer_line: Compact beside the ribs, inside their arm wrap

plausible: Flared beyond their knee with your palm down
Across their collarbone with the elbow still outside
trap: Near their hip with your wrist alone on the chest

flashcards.question: Escape Zombie Control (top): What must happen before you lift the chest?
flashcards.answer: Posture recovery follows arm clearance and an opened high leg; the hand pummel alone does not release the upper body.
flashcards.answer_line: Free the arm and reduce the high-leg connection

plausible: Move only your hand while the shoulder stays fixed
Widen the knees while the neck remains enclosed
trap: Lift the chest after arm recovery with the high leg still taut
